source: src/live.md (old Notion page 'CUTLASS, cuBLAS, cuDNN, and tensor cores', last edited 2026-09-22, fetched 2026-10-05)

facts.claim: Resources: CUTLASS documentation (~2h) and NVIDIA/cutlass repo (~45 min); 4.x docs cover C++ and CuTe DSL incl. tcgen05 guides
facts.verdict: verified (links 200, 2026-10-05)

facts.claim: Resource: Colfax Research CUTLASS tutorial series (~6h)
facts.verdict: verified (link 200); two tutorial links added

facts.claim: Resource: GPU MODE lectures (~1h30 each, ~4h30 for the CUTLASS set)
facts.verdict: kept (link 200; durations from the old page)

facts.claim: Resource: cuBLAS docs (~1h30, cuBLASLt section) and cuDNN docs (~1h30, graph API)
facts.verdict: verified (links 200)

facts.claim: Resource: PTX ISA (~1h for mma sections)
facts.verdict: verified (link 200)

facts.claim: cuBLAS: closed-source BLAS, cublasGemmEx; default GEMM; what torch.matmul calls
facts.verdict: verified (PyTorch 2.14.1 Context.cpp blasDefaultBackend = Cublas on NVIDIA)

facts.claim: cuBLASLt: descriptors, heuristic search, epilogue fusion (bias, GELU/ReLU, dGELU, aux outputs), FP8/FP4 scaling
facts.verdict: verified (cublasLt.h 13.8 enums; program compiled)

facts.claim: PyTorch uses cuBLASLt for addmm and FP8 (_scaled_mm)
facts.verdict: verified and made precise (isInputCompliesAddmmCudaLt conditions; ScaledBlas.cpp recipes)

facts.claim: cuDNN: conv, attention, norms; graph API, backend picks/fuses engines
facts.verdict: verified (cuDNN graph API docs; frontend 1.30.0 module probed)

facts.claim: cuDNN is the fastest attention on datacenter GPUs and the SDPA backend on Hopper/Blackwell
facts.verdict: corrected: cuDNN is first in SDPA's order on CC 9.x/10.x with cuDNN > 9.15 (sdp_utils.cpp); not on sm_120; 'fastest' unconfirmed (not measured here)

facts.claim: CUTLASS: open-source templates for GEMM/conv/attention; for new dtypes, fused mainloops, grouped/MoE GEMM, custom epilogues; reference for peak kernels
facts.verdict: verified (CUTLASS 4.8.0 cloned and compiled)

facts.claim: CuTe: Layout (shape:stride) and Tensor, MMA/Copy atoms; vocabulary of modern CUTLASS
facts.verdict: verified (layouts printed by CuTe, 21 cases)

facts.claim: CuTe DSL: Python, JIT-compiled
facts.verdict: verified (nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0 compiled a kernel to sm_90a PTX without a GPU)

facts.claim: CuTe DSL: near-parity performance with C++
facts.verdict: unconfirmed (no GPU to measure); not repeated

facts.claim: CuTe DSL integrates with PyTorch via DLPack
facts.verdict: verified (cutlass.cute.runtime.from_dlpack used in our script)

facts.claim: New NVIDIA example kernels ship in the CuTe DSL since 2025
facts.verdict: partly verified (examples/python/CuTeDSL in 4.8.0); date not checked

facts.claim: CCCL = Thrust, CUB, libcudacxx; never hand-write a production reduction/scan/sort
facts.verdict: kept; depth left to Writing kernels (CUB) and the root's library table

facts.claim: Triton/Gluon is the pragmatic middle for custom ML kernels
facts.verdict: kept; left to the Triton and Gluon sibling

facts.claim: Decision rule: torch.compile/cuBLAS/cuDNN first; Triton for fusion; CUTLASS/CuTe when GEMM-shaped and >90% of peak or features Triton lacks; raw PTX essentially never
facts.verdict: kept as a table

facts.claim: Tensor cores compute a small tile MMA per instruction (e.g. 16x8x16) per warp or larger
facts.verdict: verified (compiled)

facts.claim: Ladder: cuBLAS/cuDNN, Triton tl.dot, CUTLASS/CuTe atoms, wmma, PTX mma.sync/wgmma/tcgen05
facts.verdict: verified

facts.claim: wmma is portable but slow, ignore
facts.verdict: refined: wmma compiles to the same HMMA.16816 (root k6); it is limited (opaque fragments, no wgmma/tcgen05), not slower per instruction

facts.claim: Ampere sm_80: warp-level mma.sync on registers; cp.async enabling pipelining; FP16/BF16/TF32/INT8
facts.verdict: verified (HMMA.16816, HMMA.1688.TF32, IMMA.16832 compiled)

facts.claim: Hopper sm_90a: wgmma, 4 warps, operands from shared memory
facts.verdict: verified (HGMMA; refused on all other targets)

facts.claim: Hopper: TMA bulk async tiled copies with hardware swizzling from a descriptor
facts.verdict: verified (UTMALDG.2D compiled; CUtensorMap 128 B; encode needs the driver)

facts.claim: Hopper: thread block clusters and distributed shared memory
facts.verdict: verified (cluster kernels compile on sm_90a+, refused on sm_80/89); DSMEM itself on the programming-model sibling

facts.claim: Warp-specialised producer/consumer kernels (FlashAttention-3, CUTLASS mainloops)
facts.verdict: verified (CUTLASS example 48 SASS: USETMAXREG 40/232, HGMMA, UTMALDG)

facts.claim: FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) arrives with Hopper
facts.verdict: corrected: FP8 mma.sync needs sm_89 (Ada); Hopper added wgmma FP8 (QGMMA)

facts.claim: Datacenter Blackwell sm_100/sm_103 (B200/B300/GB200): tcgen05
facts.verdict: verified (UTCHMMA etc. on sm_100a, sm_100f, sm_103a; also sm_110a and sm_107a)

facts.claim: Blackwell tensor core is a per-SM async unit ('5th gen') with TMEM for accumulators
facts.verdict: verified (PTX ISA 9.4: 512 columns x 128 lanes x 32 bit); '5th gen' naming corrected (RTX 5090 also '5th Gen')

facts.claim: Single thread issues the MMA
facts.verdict: verified (our kernel issues it from threadIdx.x == 0)

facts.claim: Pair-SM MMA across 2 SMs
facts.verdict: verified (cta_group::2 -> UTCHMMA.2CTA; CUTLASS example 70 picked it)

facts.claim: Native MXFP8/MXFP6/MXFP4 block-scaled formats (2nd-gen Transformer Engine)
facts.verdict: verified for the instructions (kind::mxf8f6f4 -> UTCQMMA, mxf4nvf4 -> UTCOMMA); Transformer Engine naming left to Topic: hardware

facts.claim: CUTLASS 4.x and CuTe DSL are the practical way to program tcgen05; Triton reaches it; Gluon exposes TMEM
facts.verdict: CUTLASS verified (examples compiled); Triton tl.dot -> UTCHMMA verified by the root; Gluon left to the Triton sibling

facts.claim: Consumer Blackwell sm_120 (RTX 5090): no TMEM, no tcgen05, no wgmma; wgmma.fence will not assemble
facts.verdict: verified (exact ptxas errors)

facts.claim: sm_120 uses the Ampere-lineage mma.sync extended with FP8/FP6/FP4
facts.verdict: verified (QMMA E4M3, QMMA E2M1 and OMMA.SF block-scaled on sm_120a)

facts.claim: sm_120 has TMA and clusters
facts.verdict: verified; new: TMA multicast compiles only with an advisory warning and becomes a call (no multicast opcode)

facts.claim: 5090 kernels look like Ada/Ampere kernels; Hopper tutorials do not run on it
facts.verdict: verified (compiler evidence)

facts.claim: FP4 GEMMs on sm_120 are real and fast
facts.verdict: real: verified (CUTLASS example 79a compiles to OMMA.SF); fast: unconfirmed (not run)

facts.claim: DGX Spark / RTX Pro Blackwell use the same model
facts.verdict: verified (GB10 = CC 12.1, RTX PRO Blackwell = 12.0 on NVIDIA's list; sm_121a takes block-scaled FP4 mma, refuses tcgen05)

facts.claim: Ada-targeted FP8 code generally ports to sm_120
facts.verdict: verified for the instruction (QMMA.16832 E4M3 on both)

facts.claim: 'Directly relevant to Khalid's box' (RTX 5090)
facts.verdict: corrected: there is no NVIDIA GPU here (the CUDA root records this); all evidence is compiled, not run

facts.claim: Generations (4th = Hopper, 5th = datacenter Blackwell) do not map to compute capability; a suffixes required for accelerated instructions
facts.verdict: verified and extended: f (family) suffix from 10.0, with compiler evidence

facts.claim: CuTe reduces tiling/threading to layout algebra; compose and divide; same algebra for global tiles, swizzled smem, thread maps, MMA fragments
facts.verdict: verified (algebra ported and checked against CuTe)

facts.claim: CUTLASS kernel reads as local_tile, local_partition / ThrMMA, then copy and gemm
facts.verdict: kept (API names checked in CUTLASS 4.8.0)

facts.claim: CuTe is the main learning investment; CuTe DSL makes it explorable; start with Colfax and examples/cute/tutorial
facts.verdict: kept

facts.claim: Baseline every GEMM idea against cuBLASLt with the appropriate epilogue first
facts.verdict: kept

facts.claim: On the 5090, SDPA picks flash/cuDNN; beat it only with a genuinely different algorithm
facts.verdict: kept, refined (flash-first on sm_120 in PyTorch 2.14.1)

facts.claim: Grouped GEMM (MoE), dequant-fused GEMM, block-scaled FP8/FP4 are where custom CUTLASS/CuTe-DSL work pays
facts.verdict: kept

facts.claim: Cross-references: Topic hardware for Blackwell detail; inference-and-serving for production stacks
facts.verdict: kept (GPU architecture child linked for the hardware)
